title: Clandestine Entrants: Securing Your Vehicle
whatItIs: Drivers, owners and hirers must secure goods vehicles so nobody can hide in them to enter the UK. You can be fined even if no one is found: secure, check and record.
keyFacts: Carrying a clandestine entrant: a fine of up to £10,000 per person carried, for each person responsible.
Goods vehicle not adequately secured: up to £6,000, even if no one is found, entering or leaving the UK.
Curtain-siders: a taut TIR cord or strap through all eyelets, secured with a lock, seal or other device.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT go through UK border control if you know or suspect someone is hiding in your vehicle.

keyFacts: Don't approach anyone hiding. Stay in the cab and contact the police, port security or Border Force.

items.title: Watch the loading
items.text: Make sure no one gets in. Can't watch? Check the vehicle as soon as you can.

items.title: Lock and seal
items.text: Padlock the doors. Note seal numbers on your checklist.

items.title: Check after every stop
items.text: Roof, fabric, seals and locks, panniers, wind break and axles.

items.title: Check and record
items.text: Repeat the checks before the UK control zone. Record every check on your checklist.

a.label: Carrying a clandestine entrant
points: Owner, hirer or driver can be fined

b.label: Vehicle not adequately secured
points: Up to £6,000, even if no one is found
Applies entering or leaving the UK

onTheTest.question: You suspect someone has got into your trailer before UK border control. What should you do?
options: Not go through; tell the police or Border Force
Open the trailer and remove them yourself
Carry on and report it on delivery
onTheTest.why: You must not go through UK border control if you suspect someone is hiding in your vehicle. Don't approach them: contact the police or Border Force.

onTheTest.question: Your curtain-sided trailer has just been loaded. How should you secure it?
options: A taut TIR cord through all eyelets, locked or sealed
Tie the curtains with spare straps
onTheTest.why: A curtain-sided vehicle is secured with a TIR cable or strap that is taut, passes through all eyelets and is secured by a lock, seal or other device.

traps: An unsecured goods vehicle alone can bring a fine: no one needs to be found.
You're not expected to climb on the roof: check it from inside, or use poles, mirrors or a phone.
Don't break a customs seal to check: record which checks you couldn't do.
